name: ContractsComponentClientFacet_OnLookupContractsByParticipant
summary: The server's answer to ContractsComponentServerFacet_LookupContractsByParticipant (0x9fc). 38-byte body: the shared two-u64 head, then the 16-byte id the request carried as its trailing field, then a 6-byte trailing block that is all zero in the one captured instance. Writer FUN_142da45e0 and reader FUN_142da4680 read exactly these three runs and nothing else, which is what accounts for 16+16+6 = 38 against the 42-byte record.
purpose: Return the contracts the requesting participant may look up. The captured instance carries no contract payload at all, so what a non-empty answer looks like is unmeasured; the 6-byte trailing block is the only candidate site for it and is all zero here.

created_when: the server answers a 0x9fc lookup for a participant
lifecycle.if_absent: the contracts lookup the client asked for is never answered

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the wide prefix varint a6 23, i.e. type index 2278 = 0x8e6. fields[] below use BODY offsets, so the first body byte is at 0x00 and the 42-byte record starts 4 bytes earlier.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured 4c 0c 0e d6 47 8a 69 da = 0x4c0c0ed6478a69da. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id. In this direction the sender is the server-side contracts facet, and the value equals the local id the client's own 0x9fc request carried in its head, which is the request/response correlation: same component, same session, one id. The first u64 of the head is named in msg.time-sync-to-client.json from the decompiled writer FUN_1414dbca0 and the registry key FUN_1416c1c40.
fields.provenance: measured corpus-wide on 2026-11-09: the head appears in 36 of 138 R records across 10 wire types, one local id per component; 0x8e6 and 0x9fc share 4c0c0ed6478a69da

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Measured bf 85 31 4b bc 4a 95 1a = 0xbf85314bbc4a951a. Second u64 of the shared head: the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id, written big-endian. Read little-endian those eight bytes are 1a954abc4b3185bf, the front half of the actor id ClientAddEntryMsg (0xa4) hands the client.
fields.provenance: already earned in msg.time-sync-to-client.json (writer FUN_1414dbca0 via htonl64 FUN_1461668a0); re-measured across 10 wire types

fields.name: lookup_id
fields.note: Measured e1 63 43 70 30 7b 4d 06 a7 2f d9 df 00 5c d9 42. This is the strongest fact in the card: the same 16 bytes are the TRAILING field of the client's own 0x9fc request for this lookup, and they appear nowhere else in the 138-record corpus. So the response echoes an id the request supplied. The decompiled reader FUN_142da4680 carries it as a bare raw run, 16 bytes, from object +0x90, and the generic raw-run primitive names nothing, so the meaning stays unnamed: it may be the looked-up participant rather than the caller, and no measurement distinguishes those. It is NOT the player actor id (that is the head's second u64) and NOT the 0x9fc participant_id (1a954abc4b3185bfbe37c3d8592618e0).
fields.provenance: capture: 0x43_T0x8e6_R.bin body[0x10..0x20] vs 0x3b_T0x9fc_W.bin trailing field; cross-referenced in msg.contracts-lookup-contracts-by-participant.json

fields.name: trailing_block
fields.note: Measured 00 00 00 00 00 00 in the one captured instance. The codec that reads it, reached from FUN_142da4680, reads a prefix-varint count and then a small scalar suffix, and six bytes is exactly what the captured record leaves after head and id; but with every byte zero the internal split is not pinned by data, so the field is carried as one fixed 6-byte run rather than as a guessed count plus elements. This is the only site an actual contract payload could occupy, and it is empty here: the captured answer returns nothing.
fields.provenance: capture: 0x43_T0x8e6_R.bin body[0x20..0x26], all zero; width pinned by writer FUN_142da45e0 and reader FUN_142da4680 both ending after it
